module.name: no-literal-unions
module.description: Report literal unions for manual migration to enums.

scenarios.name: should allow a type alias that references an enum
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should allow a union of non-literal types
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should allow property literal unions handled by the property-specific rule
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the property signature
scenarios.then: no violation is reported by this rule

scenarios.name: should allow literal unions inside built-in TypeScript utility types
scenarios.given: type PublicUser = Omit<User, 'password' | 'token'> and type UsersByRole = Record<'admin' | 'guest', User>
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates literal unions inside known TypeScript utility type arguments
scenarios.then: no violation is reported because the literals describe utility-type keys or filters rather than enum domains

scenarios.name: should report literal unions inside custom generic type arguments
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the literal union inside the custom type argument
scenarios.then: a noLiteralUnions violation is reported because the exemption is limited to known TypeScript utility types

scenarios.name: should report a union of string literals
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should report a union of numeric literals
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should report a union of typeof references that resolve to string literal const values
scenarios.given: const Active = 'active'; const Inactive = 'inactive'; type Status = typeof Active | typeof Inactive
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should report an exported union of typeof references that resolve to string literal const values
scenarios.given: const Active = 'active'; const Inactive = 'inactive'; export type Status = typeof Active | typeof Inactive
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should report a union of typeof references that resolve through no-substitution template literal const values
scenarios.given: const Active = `active`; type Status = typeof Active | 'inactive'
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should allow a non-exported union of typeof references that resolve to the full boolean domain
scenarios.given: const Enabled = true; const Disabled = false; type Toggle = typeof Enabled | typeof Disabled
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should allow an exported union of typeof references that resolve to the full boolean domain
scenarios.given: const Enabled = true; const Disabled = false; export type Toggle = typeof Enabled | typeof Disabled
scenarios.when: the rule evaluates the type alias

scenarios.name: should preserve existing literal assignments and parameter contracts
scenarios.given: a string union is used by a variable or function parameter
scenarios.when: ESLint evaluates the rule or applies its offered fix
scenarios.then: a violation is reported and source text is unchanged so the valid TypeScript still compiles

scenarios.name: should keep constant lookup isolated between files
scenarios.given: one file defines string constants and another refers to undeclared identifiers with the same names
scenarios.when: ESLint evaluates the rule or applies its offered fix
scenarios.then: only the file with locally resolved literal constants is reported; no lookup state is reused

scenarios.name: should preserve value bindings during a manual enum migration
scenarios.given: a type alias has the same name as an existing runtime binding
scenarios.when: ESLint evaluates the rule or applies its offered fix
scenarios.then: the rule reports the union without introducing a colliding enum value
